subject.title: [Feature]: Add bounded/validated append semantics for pre-compaction memory flush

question: Should OpenClaw accept a built-in fail-closed daily-memory append policy for memory-triggered writes to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`, or require an opt-in/config/plugin-hook design first?
rationale: The source issue is real, but the permanent behavior changes a silent runtime memory boundary and may reject content that older sessions would have appended, so automation should not choose the strictness or hook/security model alone.

options.title: Accept Narrow Built-In Guard
options.body: Refresh and review the linked PR or successor as the preferred path: built-in caps, scaffold rejection, duplicate skipping, and telemetry for canonical daily-memory flushes only.

options.title: Require Opt-In Policy
options.body: Keep current append behavior as default and ask for an explicit config or plugin API design before any stricter validation ships.

options.title: Pause For Broader Memory API
options.body: Defer this issue into the broader bounded-memory-tool discussion if maintainers want one generalized memory write contract instead of a daily-memory-specific runtime guard.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Built-In Guard
recommendation.body: Refresh and review the linked PR or successor as the preferred path: built-in caps, scaffold rejection, duplicate skipping, and telemetry for canonical daily-memory flushes only.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` introduced the memory-flush feature and later moved ownership into the memory plugin, so this product-boundary decision is closest to that history.
